metadata.topic: Cell Biology — Bacterial Cell Structures and Infection
metadata.note: 6 marks for 3 structure explanations (2 marks each). Pili/fimbriae is given as an example. Students explain how Flagellum, Slime capsule, and Cell wall each help bacteria infect organisms. Graded as key-phrase matching. Original question requires written explanations; this model uses keyword-anchored structured_text with 2 sub-fields per structure.

question.name: CSEC Bio May 2023 Q1b(ii) — Bacterial Structures and Infection Benefits
question.text:
The diagram in Figure 2 shows the general structure of a bacterial cell (bacillus shape) with the following structures labelled:

  • Outer layers: cell membrane, cell wall, slime capsule
  • Appendages: pili/fimbriae (short hair-like projections), flagella (long whip-like tails)
  • Internal: nucleoid (circular DNA), plasmids, ribosomes

Table 1 lists four structures. The first row is completed as an example:

Pili or fimbriae → Protect bacterial cell from being eaten by phagocytes so the bacteria continue to survive and multiply.

Complete the table by explaining how EACH of the following structures helps the bacterium to infect organisms. (6 marks)
question.general_feedback:
Model answers (2 marks per structure — 1 for mechanism + 1 for benefit/consequence):

Flagellum: Provides motility (allows the bacterium to move / swim). This enables it to reach and penetrate host cells / target organs / navigate through body fluids to reach the site of infection.

Slime capsule: Protects the bacterium from being engulfed by phagocytes (white blood cells) of the host immune system. This allows bacteria to survive and multiply within the host / helps bacteria adhere to host cell surfaces.

Cell wall: Provides structural support and maintains the shape of the bacterium. Protects the cell from osmotic pressure / from bursting in hypotonic environments / from host antibodies, allowing bacteria to survive and remain infectious.

Explain how the Flagellum helps bacteria to infect organisms. (2 marks: 1 for mechanism + 1 for benefit)
Explain how the Slime capsule helps bacteria to infect organisms. (2 marks: 1 for mechanism + 1 for benefit)
Explain how the Cell wall helps bacteria to infect organisms. (2 marks: 1 for mechanism + 1 for benefit)

fields.label: Flagellum — how it works (mechanism): _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: The flagellum is a whip-like tail that spins to propel the bacterium — it provides movement/motility.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: The flagellum's function is locomotion — it rotates like a propeller to allow the bacterium to swim/move through fluids.

fields.label: Flagellum — benefit to infection (consequence): _____
fields.expected: Allows bacteria to reach host cells / infection site
fields.diagnostic_hint: Movement allows the bacterium to navigate to host cells/organs or the site of infection.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Explain WHY movement is useful for infection: it allows bacteria to reach/penetrate host tissue or navigate to target sites in the body.

options.Allows bacteria to reach host cells / in: Allows bacteria to reach host cells / infection site
options.Allows bacteria to survive and multiply: Allows bacteria to survive and multiply in the host
options.Maintains bacterial integrity inside the: Maintains bacterial integrity inside the host

fields.label: Slime capsule — how it works (mechanism): _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: The slime capsule makes the bacterium difficult to engulf (phagocytose) — it protects against the host's immune system.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: The slime capsule is a thick protective layer that prevents phagocytes (white blood cells) from engulfing and destroying the bacterium.

fields.label: Slime capsule — benefit to infection (consequence): _____
fields.expected: Allows bacteria to survive and multiply in the host
fields.diagnostic_hint: Escaping phagocytosis allows bacteria to survive and multiply inside the host, prolonging and worsening infection.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: State the consequence: because the capsule protects from phagocytes, bacteria can survive and multiply inside the host / remain infective for longer.

options.Allows bacteria to survive and multiply: Allows bacteria to survive and multiply in the host

fields.label: Cell wall — how it works (mechanism): _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: The cell wall provides structural support and protects the bacterium from osmotic pressure (bursting).

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: The cell wall maintains cell shape and resists osmotic pressure — it prevents the bacterial cell from swelling and bursting in hypotonic environments.

fields.label: Cell wall — benefit to infection (consequence): _____
fields.expected: Maintains bacterial integrity inside the host
fields.diagnostic_hint: By maintaining structural integrity, the cell wall keeps the bacterium alive in the hostile body environment, allowing it to continue infecting the host.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: State the consequence: the rigid wall keeps bacteria intact and viable inside the host / protects them from the host's defensive environment, allowing infection to continue.
